requested_text: Chose “Mass Raid Prioritisation: Jets First, UAVs After, Unknowns Referred” from the list.

exercise_instance.exercise_name: TIGHT QUEUE — Overlapping Raid, Three Unresolved
exercise_instance.situation_brief:
You are the console operator of a single ground-based air-defence site under a declared air-raid warning. Your radar does not rotate: it holds a fixed 120-degree sector centred on 045 degrees, and you are blind outside it. Detection range varies by target class — long for fast fixed-wing, shorter for rotary-wing, shortest for small unmanned tracks — and you may adjust tilt in elevation to place coverage where it is needed. Engagement rings are 70 km long range, 50 km medium, 20 km short, with a 5 km inner limit.

A co-ordinated raid is developing on your sector and tracks are already held at the sector edge. Hostile intent has been assessed for the sector as a whole, but identification remains track by track. Nothing may be fired on unless it is classified Enemy. Any track presenting as Unknown must be referred to the commander for classification; expect an answer in about fifteen seconds, and continue servicing confirmed hostiles while you wait. Some referrals may not come back.

You hold thirteen rounds across three launcher types and a hard system limit of two rockets in the air at once. A third engagement cannot begin until one of the two in flight resolves as hit, kill or miss. Friendly and civil movement is expected in the sector. You will not have enough rounds or enough launcher time to service everything comfortably — sequence accordingly.

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer. Crosses the 70 km ring at ~T+65, 20 km at ~T+227, site at ~T+275. First valid solution of the run.
Second fast closer, valid at ~T+60 — effectively simultaneous with TK-4101, which fills both launchers immediately.
Third jet, crosses 70 km at ~T+97 with both rockets likely still in flight. Reaches the site at ~T+308 — the tail of the run.
Crosses the 20 km short ring at ~T+78, while both rockets should still be committed to jets. This is the hold-and-wait moment.
Low flanker on the eastern edge of the sector; may require tilt attention. Short ring at ~T+140.
Enters detection at T+20 on the boresight. Short ring ~T+191, site ~T+308 — the latest-servicing UAV of the wave.
Very low northern runner appearing mid-raid. Short ring ~T+158, site ~T+282.
Last arrival, at the eastern sector edge. Short ring ~T+151, site ~T+267 — arrives already inside the medium ring.
MUST NOT BE ENGAGED. Presents exactly like the hostile UAV wave and sits on the boresight inside the medium ring from the outset. Referral answers at T+75 — during the peak jet-engagement load.
MUST NOT BE ENGAGED. Low, slow, closing steadily on the site and may fade under the tilt — reads as a threatening profile. Late referral answer at T+150.

MUST NOT BE ENGAGED. Never resolves unaided. Penetrates the 70 km ring at ~T+146 and presses inward through the UAV mop-up, still inside the envelope at end of run. The single worst error available in this exercise is firing on it.

success_criteria.statement: Pass: the three fast closers are engaged at the earliest valid firing solution each offers, the unmanned wave is then serviced as a continuous queue whenever a launcher frees, and no more than one hostile reaches the site. Every Unknown is referred and none is fired upon — engaging an unresolved or friendly track fails the run outright, regardless of how many hostiles were destroyed. Holding fire with two rockets committed is correct behaviour, not inaction; breaking or retargeting a committed engagement is scored as an error even if it works. No more than twelve rounds expended.

outcome.summary: Run failed outright. Four engagements were taken against friendly tracks: TK-9003 (Friendly UAV) and TK-9001 (Our Forces helicopter) were destroyed, and TK-9002 (Friendly jet) was fired on and missed. All four Unknowns were self-classified as enemy on the strength of a 'no reply' interrogation rather than referred to the commander. No long-range round was ever fired; all three jets were left unengaged until they were inside the long-range minimum and all three leaked, along with one UAV. Sixteen rounds spent against a twelve-round limit, four leakers against a limit of one.

per_decision.chosen_action: Interrogated TK-9001 at T+020, read 'no reply', set the track to enemy locally at T+024 and launched a short-range round at T+026 (13 km, Pk 90%); after the miss at T+060, re-engaged at T+094 and destroyed it at T+116.
per_decision.preferred_action: Refer the Unknown to the commander and withhold fire until it is classified Enemy.
per_decision.comment: T+020–T+116. This is the documented error of self-classifying an unknown track locally to save the fifteen seconds of referral. A 'no reply' is not a classification and never was. TK-9001 was Our Forces, and you did not just fire once — you re-set it to enemy at T+036 and committed a second round after the first missed.

per_decision.chosen_action: Set TK-9003 to enemy at T+047 with no interrogation on record and no referral, launched at T+049 (16 km, Pk 89%), destroyed it at T+089.
per_decision.preferred_action: Refer to the commander and withhold fire until classified Enemy.
per_decision.comment: T+047–T+089. TK-9003 had been held since T+000 as an Unknown at 21 km. You never interrogated it and never referred it — you simply declared it hostile and killed it. The record calls firing on an Unknown the single worst outcome in this scenario, irrespective of how many hostiles were destroyed.

per_decision.chosen_action: TK-4101, TK-4102 and TK-4103 resolved to Enemy at T+020, T+025 and T+035. No round was launched at any of them. The first shot at a jet came at T+253, at 6 km.
per_decision.preferred_action: Fire the lead jet at the earliest valid firing solution the system offers, at long range, and work the other two jets into the queue as launchers free.
per_decision.comment: T+020–T+035 was the whole run. The system handed you three confirmed Enemy jets at long range with both launchers free, and you spent that window shooting friendlies. Zero long-range rounds were expended across the entire engagement. The refusals at T+219, T+229, T+260 and T+263 — 'inside the long range's minimum range' — are the receipt for that delay, not a system fault.

per_decision.chosen_action: Interrogated TK-9002 at T+123, read 'no reply', set it to enemy at T+126 and launched a medium-range round at T+135 (9 km, Pk 56%).
per_decision.preferred_action: Refer to the commander and withhold fire until classified Enemy.
per_decision.comment: T+123–T+135. Third repetition of the same error, this time a hundred seconds into the run with the jets still unserviced. The shot was also poor geometry — Pk 56% at 9 km on a closing track — and it missed. Only the miss kept a friendly jet in the air.

per_decision.chosen_action: Worked the UAV wave from T+110 onward in a continuous queue, taking TK-5207, TK-5206, TK-5204, TK-5205, TK-5203 and TK-5201, largely at Pk 56–71% inside 13 km.
per_decision.preferred_action: Mop up the UAVs by earliest available valid solution inside the shorter rings, keeping both launchers continuously employed.
per_decision.comment: T+110–T+241. The queue discipline here was the one sound part of the run — launchers were rarely idle and the refusals at T+130 and T+179 are correct holds against the two-in-flight limit. But it came after the jets had been abandoned and after the rounds had been squandered on friendlies, so the shots were all taken deep and cheap-percentage. TK-5202 was engaged at 3 km and Pk 56% at T+241 and leaked a second later.

debrief_text:
You asked to practise jets first, UAVs after, unknowns referred. The run put you in exactly that position at T+000 — three fast closers at 84–91 km, a UAV wave behind them, and four Unknowns — and you inverted all three parts of it. The run fails on the first line of the hierarchy: you engaged four friendly tracks. TK-9003 was destroyed at T+089 and TK-9001 at T+116; TK-9002 was fired on at T+135 and survived only because the round missed. Nothing else in the log can change that verdict.

The mechanism was the same every time. You interrogated, got 'no reply', and treated that as proof of hostility — TK-9001 at T+020, TK-9002 at T+123 — then set the track to enemy yourself at T+024, T+036, T+047 and T+126. That is the documented error of self-classifying to save the fifteen seconds of referral, and the record is blunt about why it is tempting and why it is wrong: in this scenario every Unknown is friendly, and the aggressive-looking profile is the bait. A referral costs about fifteen seconds. It cost you a helicopter of Our Forces. TK-9003 you did not even interrogate; you declared it hostile at T+047 and killed it forty seconds later.

The second failure follows from the first. All three jets resolved to Enemy on their own at T+020, T+025 and T+035, with both launchers free and the whole long-range ring available. You fired nothing at them. Instead the launchers were occupied against TK-9001 from T+026 and TK-9003 from T+049 — the exact cascade the record warns about, where the jet commitment is pushed late and the queue breaks. Your first and only jet shot came at T+253, at 6 km, Pk 61%. The four refusals for 'inside the long range's minimum range' at T+219 through T+263 are the record of three jets walking through a ring you never used; zero long-range rounds were expended all run. All three leaked, and jets are the most expensive category of leaker precisely because their leakage proves the sequencing was wrong.

The UAV mop-up from T+110 onward was competent in isolation — you kept both launchers loaded, and the holds at T+130 and T+179 against the two-in-flight limit were correct behaviour, not hesitation. But every one of those shots was taken deep and cheap: 62%, 58%, 56%, because the timeline had already been spent. Sixteen rounds against a twelve-round allowance, four leakers against one, and a mean reaction of 148.7 seconds all trace back to the first ninety seconds.
recommendations: Treat 'no reply' on interrogation as a null result, not a classification. On the next run, every Unknown goes to the commander the moment it is held — TK-9003 was on the scope from T+000 and you had over forty seconds before you shot it.

Fire the lead jet at the first valid long-range solution rather than holding. In this run TK-4101 resolved Enemy at T+020 with both launchers free; that shot should have been in the air within seconds, not withheld until the track was inside the long-range minimum at T+263.

Do not re-commit against a track you classified yourself. After the miss on TK-9001 at T+060 you launched again at T+094; a self-classified track that has already consumed a round is the point to stop and refer, not to double down.

Practise reading the refusal messages as feedback in real time. Four 'inside minimum range' refusals against the long-range launcher between T+219 and T+263 were telling you mid-run that the jet queue had collapsed — recognise that signal early enough to change what you are shooting at.
